creator: kamchai
summary: A fast Thai explainer about a product or tool, built on a split screen. B-roll fills the top half and the seated speaker (mic in shot, bookshelf behind) sits in the bottom half. The hook opens split, with a 2-3 row Thai headline in heavy white type (one phrase in yellow) just above the seam and the product's name on the footage. It ends with the first layout switch at 2.5-7.7 s. The body then alternates blocks of 2.5-8.6 s: split blocks carry one-line seam captions on a dark strip, full-speaker blocks carry a big chest punch phrase and sometimes a yellow label above the head, and one reel adds full-frame cutaways with a centred phrase. The speaker's shot is cut 30-38 times a minute in the body (median shot 1.4-1.6 s). About half to three quarters of those cuts are jump cuts of the speaker and about 30 % are layout switches. B-roll swaps without a speaker cut add 0-12 more per minute. The voice has no pauses, and one reel ends on a comment-keyword CTA with the handle.

fit_notes: The split needs footage for about half the reel. With no product footage, use stock only for illustrative shots and mark product-label 'ask'.
Reach 26-43 shot cuts/min in the body with take boundaries and zoom.snaps at sentence starts. Changing the B-roll does not raise the shot-cut rate.
Thai rows: break only at phrase ends; seam captions at most 17 chars/s and 35 chars per line.
